messages:
andrew: Ran nsys on the serve binary with a forced small-batch workload. Timeline looks weird — lots of H2D memcpy on stream 2 that seems to serialize kernel launches on stream 0. Here's the command and a short summary.

andrew: command: ```nsys profile --output=~/traces/trace_1768684321 --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn,osrt --sample=none ./serve --mode=benchmark --batch-size=1 --steps=200```

andrew: Findings: memcpy (host->device) shows as long contiguous blocks (10-20ms) interleaved with tiny kernels (<1ms). CPU saw scheduling gaps aligning with those memcpy blocks. KV cache hits correlate with no memcpy; misses cause memcpy + small copy kernels per layer.

sara: interesting — are we using pageable host memory? That would cause synchronous staging and stall default stream. Did you try cudaHostAlloc or cudaMemcpyAsync on a different stream?

andrew: We were using ordinary malloc + cudaMemcpyAsync on stream 2. But nsys timeline shows the memcpy in default stream semantics — suspect driver is promoting async to sync because memory not pinned.

ben: +1. If the host pointer is pageable, cudaMemcpyAsync falls back to sync behind the scenes. Try cudaHostAlloc(..., cudaHostAllocMapped) or at least cudamemcpyAsync with pinned memory. Also verify stream flags (non-blocking) when creating streams.

andrew: Quick patch: changed batch input allocator to use pinned buffers (cudaHostAlloc) and re-ran. Memcpy blocks shrank to ~1-2ms and kernels overlapped much better. Throughput +27% for small-batch workload.

alix: nice. Did you also profile NVTX ranges for KV lookup vs decode? Need to see if KV cache misses are causing many small memcopies between host and device per token.

andrew: yes — NVTX showed KV miss path does a host fetch then a cudaMemcpy to device for the KV slice, done per token. That's the culprit. Plan: refactor to prefetch upcoming KV slices into a device ring buffer and issue async copies earlier (prefetch window = 8 tokens) so copies can overlap with compute.

sara: Also look at kernel selection: small sequence lengths end up triggering a different kernel path with higher kernel launch overhead. Maybe enable small-kernel batching (coalesce multiple requests into grouped launch) or switch to persistent kernels.

ben: For the memcpy vs kernel overlap, another trick is to use cudaMemcpyAsync into device staging buffer on a separate stream, then use cudaEventRecord + cudaStreamWaitEvent to sync only when needed so H2D doesn't block compute stream. Also double-check L2 caching behavior on our A100 variant — small slices can thrash L2 and make kernels slower.

andrew: Repro steps + trace link: https://internal-traces/redwood/1768684321.nsys.qd (trace uploaded). Will try prefetch ring and pinned allocator change in the same PR.

perf-bot: perf/regression check queued for PR #4221 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alix: If you want, I can pair for a perf run tomorrow. Also collect CPU perf (perf tool) because there are scheduling gaps that might be from Python GIL holding processes while we prepare H2D copies.

andrew: thanks — will add perf (topdown) and a perfetto user-space trace to capture thread wakeups. Pushed branch: pr/4221-kv-prefetch.

sara: ✅ great. Please include before/after nsight screenshots and a short kernel timeline snippet in the PR description; they help reviewers understand overlap improvements.
